approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic molecular search guided by a Gaussian process fitted only to this session’s accepted scores. It uses count fingerprints and a generalized Tanimoto kernel, with the observed-score mean and scale restoring predictions to score units. For each announced batch the breeder constructs a fresh field of 160 molecules using ranked parent selection, graph crossover and short sampled mutation chains. Canonical identity checks, duplicate rejection and the inherited sulfur rule govern admission. The allocator draws one correlated posterior function row per batch position, takes the largest still-available value and excludes that selected identity from later positions. After three non-improving batches, only the forty highest original posterior means are eligible; the full field returns after an improving batch. Actual feedback updates the complete archive and the population of the sixty-four best scored molecules. The dormant rejection-conditioned mutation floor is already absent.
approach.novelty: Replace the batch’s sequence of Thompson winners with probability-of-optimality allocation: count which eligible molecule wins each of 10,000 correlated posterior draws, then buy the announced number with the largest counts. Each draw votes over the same fixed eligible field, so a batch’s captured winner probability is the sum of its members’ frequencies. The scientific prediction is that this different use of the existing posterior changes paid identities and captures more of that probability mass, which may convert into larger real gains. The same-Parent siblings tested mutation-continuation removal, restricted mean or correlation removal, local-model control, and a persistent tree replacement; none tested this batch objective. Earlier expected-improvement and fantasy-conditioning experiments priced improvement magnitude or changed later covariance. This intervention keeps the original posterior and eligibility while changing the winner-probability objective.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is conversion of a useful correlated predictor and broad generated field into substantial paid incumbent gains. The actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de completes all fifteen Search sessions with mean 0.607030316211131 and seed standard deviation 0.030175277546149237; its seed macros are 0.649701282562401, 0.585233817344553 and 0.586155848726439. Its fresh 160-member fields and successful posterior selections supply 435 batches and 4,350 paid proposals, including 88 restricted batches in thirteen sessions, without posterior fallback. Read the accepted nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/summary.json, seed-1/summary.json and seed-2/summary.json and their run.log files; policy/scratch/r0058-00-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json indexes the fifteen per-task audits with exact underlying trajectory/log paths and hashes. Parent paid full/late incumbent-increment mass is 5.978073077532332 / 1.0224077547621127, with late meaning optimizer ordinals 146 through 290 and denominators 4,350 / 2,175. The retained within-set mean has applicable positive conditional evidence: n-8e00e5e9fc34 removes that consumer and loses 0.023092425745076712; n-5e03d3ccd1b7 removes only restricted residual correlation and loses 0.008352681729073996. Those results support keeping the fitted mean/covariance, not a guarantee of any new acquisition objective. Counterexamples remain direct: n-8a62df15e51f correctly improves its shared-panel incumbent-referenced expected-improvement utility but loses 0.05627557001043134 against its own code Parent; n-698a02f85be1 correctly executes calibrated EI plus mean-fantasy covariance deflation but loses 0.05328817319169632 on its historical masked host. Thus fewer noisy row decisions, more diversity, and better model-objective values are not independently established bottleneck cures. The specific open test is whether maximizing the empirical probability of including a current eligible-field winner reallocates actual purchases usefully. It requires no claim that the Parent lacks covariance, mean guidance, valid supply, or a functioning stall rule.

method_change.previous_method: Independent correlated Thompson row winners, sequentially masked within the inherited fresh field and stall-conditioned eligibility.
method_change.proposed_method: qPO: top winner-frequency batch over one fixed eligible field using exactly 10,000 joint latent posterior samples and original-mean/index ties.
method_change.rationale: Actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de supplies a functioning fresh field and joint posterior. Its restricted mean and covariance consumers have useful conditional evidence, but prior acquisition changes did not convert model utility into paid gains. This component change tests a different, source-backed additive winner-event objective while retaining those measured capabilities and all generator/feedback laws.

hypothesis: On each successful allocation from actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, hold the inherited pool order, original raw-score mean mu, score scale s, standardized latent covariance C, actual successful jitter j and full Cholesky factor L fixed. Keep the original eligible set E: all pool indices, or the exact inherited top-forty mean mask when its existing stall predicate is active. Generate exactly R=10,000 joint latent rows F[r,i]=mu[i]+s*(Z@L.T)[r,i]. Draw Z first at the inherited (announced_batch_size,len(pool)) shape and then at (10000-announced_batch_size,len(pool)) from the same existing generator, in that order. For each row assign one winner w[r]=min argmax over original indices in E, and let c[i]=sum_r 1[w[r]=i]. Choose the announced batch by sorting E once by (-c[i],-mu[i],i). The domain E remains fixed for every winner count; selecting a member does not remove it from later winner events and does not condition covariance or introduce a fantasy label. An exact zero count is a valid finite-panel result: it is filled by the same original-mean then index rule, never an adaptive sample-budget change or a fallback. For selected set S, M(S)=sum_{i in S} c[i]/10000 is the empirical probability that a single row winner lies in S. The active top-count set must weakly maximize M among all feasible batches. Compared with the complete passive original Thompson batch on the first rows and its own availability masks, predict at least one changed paid set and strictly positive aggregate captured-mass gain. That is a finite-panel allocation prediction, not a calibrated chemical-optimality or global-optimum claim. Higher full/late useful paid gain is a separate downstream prediction. The extra allocation RNG advance is intrinsic to this registered construction; there is no assertion of matching later Parent/Child random states or adaptive histories.

finding_summary.headline: qPO captures more winner probability, but total progress and final scores fall
finding_summary.insights: The borrowed winner-frequency and top-probability batch construction both operated faithfully. Their transfer is limited to the inherited latent posterior and each freshly generated eligible field; this does not test the paper’s observation posterior, fixed-library setting or global-optimum guarantee. The loss cannot be explained by wholesale failure to sample or by mean/index completion dominating allocation: the median field has 118 positive-count candidates, only 11 of 4,350 selections have zero counts, and the two 5,000-draw halves share an average 9.06 of ten selected members. Some estimator uncertainty remains—283 of 435 half-panel sets differ—but this experiment does not identify its causal cost. The deeper limitation is useful conversion. Within purchased batches, winner probability has mean rank correlation 0.178 with realized scores, compared with 0.429 for the original predictive mean; these are selected-stream diagnostics, not measurements of unpurchased winners. Probability concentration also coexists with more similar purchases: fragment-excluded within-batch similarity rises from 0.483 to 0.524 even while typed/generic scaffold counts grow from 1,667/951 to 1,982/1,203. This supports a diagnosis of continued local refinement and motif growth within the current search, rather than global scaffold collapse. The size tails remain costly: all 143 purchases below twelve heavy atoms contribute zero incumbent gain, and the above-fifty tail grows from 44 to 194 purchases while contributing only 0.04996 gain. Changed-to molecules do survive and breed, so a missing feedback path is ruled out; their lineage does not reveal the scores of displaced alternatives. A different ranking model aligned with realized gain, or a proposal/search method that sustains useful distinct molecular frameworks, could address these limitations; neither is established as a remedy here. The result settles activation of this frozen configuration and rejects its full-run benefit prediction on this panel. It leaves the broader approach open and does not authorize an automatic sample-count or mask retune.
finding_summary.results: The allocation mechanism is confirmed. All 435 batches exactly reproduce the registered 10,000-draw counts and ordering, with no fallback. Average captured winner probability rises from 0.44950 for the passive original rule to 0.56646; 432 batch sets change, and 2,311 changed-to molecules receive real feedback. This is a finite-panel result on the Child’s actual states, not a score for the unpurchased alternatives. Mean final Top-1 falls from 0.60703 to 0.55804, a paired change of -0.04899; all three seed macros decline and the 0.60903 target is missed. On all 4,350 purchases, parent-beating offspring increase from 634 to 723 and incumbent updates from 253 to 300, but total incumbent-gain mass falls from 5.97807 to 5.24320. The late half improves: 96 versus 76 updates and gain mass 1.33524 versus 1.02241 on 2,175 purchases. Prospective mean-squared error on the purchased stream falls from 0.01160 to 0.00671. Thus more frequent small gains, better selected-stream error and stronger late progress do not compensate for the lost full-run progress.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families, oversized repeated scaffolds and small fragments; reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry remain common.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-0eae06e8d311 produced connected aromatic and heteroaromatic families with carbonyls, imines, amines, sulfur groups and extensive halogen substitution. Familiar medicinal-chemistry motifs coexist with N-halogen bonds, peroxide links, contracted aromatic rings and complex cages. 'Broad' describes the aggregate graph repertoire, not broad useful chemistry within every session; 'questionable' is a structural reading, not a route-feasibility measurement. The frozen comparison explicitly marks Child evaluation complete and Parent pairing complete, with Search seeds 0/1/2 and all five tasks; every listed Child and published Parent trajectory was present and read. The digest covers 900 accepted molecules per task, including 30 initial records, and 870 optimizer proposals. No task was omitted. Across 4,350 paid Child molecules versus 4,350 Parent molecules, median heavy atoms are 31 versus 28; size tails are 143 versus 124 below twelve and 194 versus 44 above fifty. Child nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 1982/1203 with coverage 4226/4350; Parent counts are 1667/951 with coverage 4255/4350. Radius-2 Morgan sparse-count mean within-batch similarity is 0.494712 versus 0.459370, and mean nearest preceding-batch archive similarity is 0.742474 versus 0.739936. Requiring both molecules to have at least twelve heavy atoms gives within-batch means 0.524489/0.482905 and nearest-archive means 0.764520/0.757735. Late paid ordinals 146-290 contain 2,175 purchases: Child/Parent below-twelve counts are 58/45 and above-fifty counts 73/3. All fragment-tail incumbent increments are zero, including late purchases. Full observed incumbent-gain sums are 5.243198882/5.978073078; late sums are 1.335237861/1.022407755. Full gains telescope to endpoints from the initial incumbents, and neither gain sums nor structural associations establish allocation causation. Audits retain every task/seed, empty group and zero-gain row. Trajectories alone do not identify paid breeding parents, survival, displaced alternatives or descendant/terminal-censoring outcomes; no such attribution is supplied here. No missing pharmacophore can be inferred uniquely from these correlated score traces, and no external target structure or reference molecule was used. Child sources remain the request-listed staging files, not an authoritative published Child archive; no copy is substituted for that provenance. All chemistry associations and transferable gaps are conditional on this node, this Parent and this Search panel.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
